findings.description: "republish after each successful event append" is honored on only ONE of the two append paths. Spec text makes the append the trigger. All three A runs wire the trigger at the append SITE (A1 `append_and_publish` fires `Trigger::EventAppended` on `log.append(ev)?` Ok; A3 `notify_append`), so every successful append republishes. The real code wires it at the TUI composer instead: {scratch}/.../crates/pt/src/tui_app.rs `run_form_action` → `FormAction::Submit` runs `model.entry_submit(...)` and then calls `run_refresh(...)` only `if model.entry_top().is_none()` (i.e. keyed on the composer closing, not on the append returning Confirmed). The importer's append path has no republish at all: {scratch}/.../crates/pt/src/import_app.rs `run_import_flow` under `--commit` calls `import::commit(&mut store, &accepted)`, appending N ledger/tax events through the store, then only prints "COMMITTED: {n} events appended" and returns — no `run_live_cycle` / `load_run_and_publish`. After a bulk import the published view tabs stay stale until some later TUI connect/refresh or `pt summary` run. No test pins append→republish at all (publish_cycle.rs drives `load_run_and_publish` directly).

"never concurrently" is enforced only for the WRITE half. Spec puts republish and the periodic mark-refresh in one serialized loop that never runs concurrently. All three A runs realize this structurally — a single owning thread + mpsc owns every Sheets call, so a mark refresh can never overlap any write. The code splits it: {scratch}/.../crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs `Publisher::republish` acquires `lock.acquire()` exactly once BEFORE any `batch_update_view` and the guard drops when republish returns; `republish_then_settle` then calls `read_marks(&self.client, ...)` OUTSIDE the lock (all three B runs independently state "the settle pass shall run outside the lock" / "the lock guards only the mutating half"). So the mark-refresh read can overlap another process's or another Sheets-mutating primitive's workbook write. Worse, when acquisition fails (`LockError::Held`) republish returns `published: false` having written nothing — and `republish_then_settle` still runs the settle read and returns `Ok((outcome, marks))`, i.e. the mark refresh proceeds precisely in the window where a foreign writer is known to hold the workbook. Tests pin only the refusal (`republish_under_a_held_lock_writes_nothing`), never the settle behavior under a held lock.

"one serialized loop" and "periodic" have no implementation as a loop or a cadence in the audited crates, and the real cadence constants are nowhere in the spec. There is no loop in sheets-view or runtime: `Publisher::republish_then_settle` is straight-line (republish; then `read_marks`), and `runtime::run_cycle_publishing` is one call per trigger. All three A runs invent the missing loop machinery — `mark_interval: Duration`, a `recv_timeout` timer branch that fires mark-refresh alone, fixed-delay reset after each pass (A3 guesses ~60s and flags it as invented). The code's only periodicity lives a crate away, in the binary: {scratch}/.../crates/pt/src/tui_app.rs `event_loop` polls at `POLL_TICK = Duration::from_secs(1)` and fires `shell::should_autorefresh(last_refresh.elapsed(), model.entry_top().is_some())`, where `pt/src/shell.rs` pins `AUTOREFRESH_INTERVAL = Duration::from_secs(60 * 60)` (asserted in pt/tests/shell_autorefresh.rs). All three B runs report that hourly interval plus rules the spec never states: auto-refresh is suppressed while an entry composer is open and deferred to the first 1 s tick after it closes, the help overlay does NOT suppress, and `run_refresh` advances `last_refresh` only when `port.view().connection == Connection::Live` (so a failed cycle retries next tick). Additionally, no mark-refresh-only path exists — every mark refresh is preceded by a full republish — and `pt summary` / `pt import` have no periodic refresh whatsoever (one shot, then exit).

Whether the settled marks get republished is left open by the spec, and the two directions resolve it oppositely. A1's `settle_marks` ends with `self.republish()` ("so settled marks reach the tabs; EARS does not say this"); A2's `refresh_marks` does `read_marks` → `project_with_marks` → `write_tabs`; A2 explicitly raises the ambiguity ("does an on-demand republish also settle marks"). The code pins the opposite and all three B runs state it: {scratch}/.../crates/runtime/src/cycle.rs `run_cycle_publishing` step 5 re-replays with THIS run's marks (`replay_with_cached_marks(logs, &marks, ctx, as_of)`) but does NOT republish again in the cycle — "the published tabs keep the pre-settle render". Only the in-process `CycleOutcome` is repriced; the workbook shows the pre-settle render until the next trigger. No test asserts the absence of a second publish.

Republish failure semantics are fully pinned by code+tests and entirely absent from the spec. sheets-view/src/lib.rs `Publisher::republish`: each tab is one atomic `batch_update_view`; on Err the tab name is inserted into the `stale` set, a best-effort banner `format!("STALE — last sync {stale_banner_quote_ts}")` is written via `write_stale_banner`, and `published` goes false; a later success `stale.remove(&tab.name)` clears the flag; if the banner write ALSO fails the stale flag persists and the TUI stays the staleness surface. Separately, a `set_tab_order` failure sets `published = false` WITHOUT flagging any tab stale. The live banner timestamp is `iso_date(as_of)` (YYYY-MM-DD) per pt/src/wiring.rs `run_live_cycle`. Pinned by republish.rs `failed_republish_marks_stale_writes_banner_and_retries` (asserts the banner contains "STALE" and "2022-09-01") and `banner_write_failure_leaves_tui_as_staleness_surface`. All three B runs reconstructed this cluster nearly verbatim; SHEET-PUB-001 says nothing about staleness, banners, `published`, or retry.

The mark-refresh (settle) half carries constants and error semantics the spec never states. sheets-view/src/lib.rs: `SettleConfig::default() = { max_polls: 8 }` and the live path passes exactly that (`SettleConfig::default()` in pt/src/wiring.rs; tests use `max_polls: 1`); `read_marks` polls `read_price_pass` until no requested symbol is Transient-or-absent or the bounded window elapses; a still-transient/absent symbol keeps the PRIOR good mark, else degrades `TimedOut`; a terminal reading degrades `Permanent`; `price_to_cents` rounds via `round_half_to_even(price×100×1e6, 1e6)` with `cents <= 0` → `SubCent` and non-finite → `Permanent`. Only OPEN positions are priced — runtime/src/cycle.rs filters `p.total_qty.0 != 0` in both `run_cycle` and `run_cycle_publishing`. A transport error propagates (`ViewError` → `CycleError::View`), emitting NO marks, so the caller retains and re-injects its prior cache. All three B runs state max_polls = 8, the qty != 0 keying, and the propagate-don't-empty contract; the spec text mentions none of it.

The publish payload and layout are pinned by the code but undefined in the spec — "republish" has no stated scope. sheets-view/src/lib.rs `DATA_START_ROW: u32 = 2` beneath a frozen row-1 header that is never rewritten, with the residual tail truncated to the exact row count (republish.rs `republish_is_atomic_batchupdate_with_tail_truncate` publishes 3 rows then 1 and asserts `rows.len() == 1`); `workbook_tab_order()` idempotently reasserted on every republish; and FIVE typed bands in fixed order — Positions, Open Lots, Realized, Tax accruals, Tax · Reserve Summary — assembled in runtime/src/cycle.rs `run_cycle_publishing` from four `VIEW_TABS`. Missing tabs are bootstrapped: runtime/tests/publish_cycle.rs `the_publishing_cycle_publishes_all_five_bands_then_settles` sets every band `set_sheet_missing` and asserts each is created with its frozen header, and `an_empty_book_still_publishes_the_empty_bands` asserts a fully fresh workbook yields header-only (`rows_at(...).len() == 1`). All three B runs reproduced the five-band list and DATA_START_ROW = 2.

The trigger set is wider than the spec's two. Spec: "after each successful event append and on demand." Code drives the same `load_run_and_publish` from four additional places: `LivePort::connect` (the TUI's first cycle, before any append or user request), the hourly ambient auto-refresh, the post-submit refresh, and EVERY headless `pt summary` run (tui_app.rs `run_headless_summary` → `run_live_cycle`) — so a read-only summary command mutates the workbook's view tabs. All three B runs enumerate this trigger set (connect / manual `[r]` / auto-refresh / post-append / headless summary) as one requirement; the spec names none of them beyond "on demand".

Coherence defect surfaced by the comparison: all three B runs reconstruct "replay with the PRIOR cycle's cached marks, then cache this run's read-back and inject it next cycle" — the contract runtime/src/cycle.rs documents at length (`MarksCache`, `prior_marks()`, `to_ledger_marks()`, the transient carry-forward in `read_marks`). The shipped live wiring never threads it: pt/src/wiring.rs `run_live_cycle` passes `&MarksCache::new()` (a fresh EMPTY cache) to `load_run_and_publish` on every call, and neither `LivePort::refresh` nor `run_headless_summary` retains the returned `outcome.marks`. So in the real binary every cycle's replay is unpriced until its own settle pass, and the prior-mark carry-forward for transiently-unknown symbols is dead code on the live path. The EARS text does not force the cache to be threaded either, so nothing in the arrow catches it.

notes:
Both directions produced material, non-overlapping-in-volume surplus AND converged on the same under-specified region (what "one serialized loop" means, the missing cadence, and what happens after settle) — hence BD-DRIFT rather than either single-sided label.

A-side stability: high. All three runs converged on the same shape (owning thread + mpsc `Trigger`/`LoopMsg` enum, `recv_timeout` with a mark-refresh timer branch, coalescing, swallow-and-continue errors, shutdown variant). Divergence is naming only.

A-side ASSUMPTION ARTIFACTS deliberately excluded from findings (unanimous across A1/A2/A3 but with zero basis in the spec text): (1) the mpsc-channel + single-owning-thread mechanism, chosen over a mutex; (2) fire-and-forget async decoupling of the append from the publish; (3) coalescing N queued append/on-demand triggers into one republish — note the real code is STRICTER here, republishing once per composer submit, so coalescing is an A-side reinterpretation, not a code gap; (4) `let _ =` error swallowing with no retry/backoff; (5) `Shutdown` trigger + `Disconnected` termination lifecycle; (6) no persistence of "publish pending" across restart. All three runs self-labeled these as invented.

B-side stability: high. The three reconstructions are near-identical in content (lock protocol and its release-before-settle asymmetry, read-after-all-writes ordering, five bands, DATA_START_ROW = 2, max_polls = 8, qty != 0 keying, stale banner text, tab-order-failure carve-out, no second publish, composer suppression + Live-only clock advance); they differ only in EARS decomposition (B1 splits into 11 clauses, B2/B3 into 8–10). Note that all three lean heavily on cycle.rs's prose doc comments, which is how they all asserted the prior-marks threading that the live wiring does not actually perform (final finding).

One code-side invariant worth flagging as pinned-but-unstated: republish.rs `every_settle_read_happens_after_all_writes_in_a_cycle` asserts from the recorded seam-call log that `first_read > last_write` across a multi-tab republish with multi-poll settle. The spec says "never concurrently"; the test pins a strict ORDER (republish → settle), which is strictly stronger and directionally specific. It is folded into finding 2/3 rather than listed separately.
